conventions.margin: Dem minus Rep, in percentage points (a Republican winning by 10 is -10).
conventions.home_state_pres2024_margin: Computed from Wikipedia 2024 presidential state results (project file pres_parsed.json, source https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_United_States_presidential_election).
conventions.overperformance_vs_baseline_pts: Computed = baseline_margin minus result_margin (both Dem minus Rep). Positive = the Republican ran AHEAD of the baseline (did better than the party's presidential showing in that state); negative = ran behind. Baseline is the most recent prior presidential margin in the state (same-day presidential margin for 2024 races). These are derived values, not reported figures.
conventions.age_in_2028: Age on Election Day, Nov 7, 2028, computed from birth dates in each person's Wikipedia biography (biographical, not a 2026 outcome; bios not re-fetched this session).
conventions.market_prob: Implied probability of winning the 2028 GOP NOMINATION, Kalshi and Polymarket quotes as aggregated by DeFi Rate, snapshot Nov 4 2026 10:09 AM ET (quotes observed 6:38-10:09 AM ET), unless noted.

third_term_talk: Trump has repeatedly teased a third term through 2026 (joked about 'eight or nine years' in May; wore a 'Trump 2028' hat and spoke of a 'fourth term' at the July 24 WHCD; said Aug 12 the 'law is very strong'). At an Oct 22, 2026 Sioux City, Iowa rally he said he believed the law bars a third term ('quite concise') but claimed a right to run because 'they cheated us'; on Nov 1 (Pod Force One) he said 'I'd love to run again, if I had the chance... But the language is very exacting.' Constitutional status: the 22nd Amendment bars anyone from being elected president more than twice; scholars say the 12th Amendment also blocks a VP-succession route (a person ineligible to be president is ineligible to be VP). Any change needs a constitutional amendment (two-thirds of each chamber or a convention, plus ratification by three-quarters of states); Speaker Mike Johnson said there is 'no path.' After the Nov 3 Democratic House and Senate takeover, an amendment is even less plausible. Rep. Andy Ogles, who proposed a 22nd Amendment change in Jan 2025, lost renomination in 2026. Markets: 'Donald Trump' for the 2028 GOP nomination at ~1.8-1.9% (Kalshi/Polymarket, Nov 4). NYT/Siena (Oct 12-19) still found 8% of likely GOP primary voters choosing Trump when offered.
